subject.title: [Security] Unsafe deserialization of incoming WebSocket commands in Gateway

question: Does any current core or plugin Gateway method handler turn attacker-controlled parsed request properties into a prototype-mutating assignment or merge?
rationale: The stated Zod-based root cause is inaccurate, but the protected security report cannot be conclusively cleared without either identifying or excluding a concrete downstream gadget across the method-handler boundary.

options.title: Confirm no reachable sink
options.body: Audit representative high-risk handlers and add a focused hostile-frame test proving prototype integrity, then close the public report with non-sensitive evidence.

options.title: Open private advisory
options.body: If a concrete method and mutation sink are found, move exploit details into a private GHSA and patch that handler or shared unsafe merge primitive.

options.title: Add parser-wide filtering
options.body: Reject restricted property names at the transport boundary only if maintainers intentionally choose that protocol rule and verify compatibility across clients and plugins.

recommendation.title: Confirm no reachable sink
recommendation.body: Audit representative high-risk handlers and add a focused hostile-frame test proving prototype integrity, then close the public report with non-sensitive evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent history is most directly associated with security-sensitive authorization and pairing hardening in this WebSocket boundary.
